features.summary: New WebRTC tests check how media streams are selected and handled, how audio-source statistics are reported, and when ICE candidate pools are gathered—including candidates obtained through a TURN relay. They also verify that the pool cannot be changed after connection setup begins, helping catch problems before they affect calls.

features.summary: WebRTC connections can now gather ICE candidates ahead of negotiation using `iceCandidatePoolSize`, potentially reducing the wait before a connection is established. The changes also add statistics about audio sources and keep each media track’s playback time and ended status up to date.

features.summary: The ICE transport layer can prepare a pool of connection candidates before WebRTC negotiation starts, helping connections get underway sooner. It also more reliably marks host candidates as ready during setup.

features.summary: The shared WebRTC layer now gathers ICE candidates in advance when requested by `iceCandidatePoolSize`. ICE candidates are possible network paths between participants, so preparing them early can reduce connection setup time.

features.summary: Remote WebRTC audio tracks now request an audio graph driven by the system clock. This helps keep their playback aligned with the browser’s audio timing.

Related changes also improve codec negotiation by leaving out details for codecs a page excluded and avoiding early media reception when no usable codecs are available; documentation about the socket process was updated.

features.summary: ICE setup is more robust when gathering cannot start or a connection encounters STUN rate limits, reducing the chance that signaling is left incomplete. The area also includes cleanup of older networking code and improvements to resource handling and networking rules.

features.summary: WebRTC media transport now runs in Firefox’s content process, removing an older socket-process bridge, and connection allowlists can block WebRTC connections that are not permitted. Remote audio clock support and sender parameter handling were also improved; the remaining changes streamline internal C++ ownership and argument handling.

features.summary: The WebRTC negotiation engine now handles unknown media types more consistently, including comparing them, reusing their session-description sections, and reserving their IDs. It also lets a remote H.264 setting for frame size or frame rate take precedence over limits implied by the codec profile, improving negotiation when peers advertise different capabilities.

features.summary: WebRTC can prepare ICE candidates before negotiation, which can shorten the wait to connect, and now reports audio-source statistics. Track timing and ended status are also kept current, while connection statistics now report the target bitrate—the planned sending rate—instead of an older byte-count measure.

features.summary: WebRTC senders now support the `keyFrame` encoding option in `RTCRtpSender.setParameters`, allowing a page to request a key frame—an independently decodable video frame. Firefox also updates audio synchronization in place and recreates a send stream when its media-section ID changes, helping keep sending behavior correct during renegotiation.

features.summary: Firefox’s SDP (Session Description Protocol), which describes a WebRTC session’s media and connection settings, was updated to a newer version. Answers now explicitly disable unknown media types while preserving support for recognizing and handling them, helping negotiation remain compatible when peers use unfamiliar media.

features.summary: Video frames decoded by libwebrtc are now painted using the color space they declare, helping colors appear as intended. The change also updates internal handling of the buffers used to pass frame data.
